# task-cf69f9ec: fill interiors of closed rectangular frames

## When to use
Use on task id `task-cf69f9ec` when a sparse orthogonal scaffold forms one or more rectangular outlines. The outline and surrounding/background colors are not fixed across instances; identify them from the current grid rather than assuming color 5 on 9. In observed instances, strictly interior cells of each fully closed rectangle are recolored to 4. Preserve the outline and everything outside those interiors.

## General procedure
1. Find candidate axis-aligned rectangular outlines made from a consistent scaffold color. A rectangle qualifies only if its full top, bottom, left, and right sides are continuously present.
2. For every qualifying rectangle spanning rows `r1..r2` and columns `c1..c2`, change only strict interior coordinates `r1+1..r2-1`, `c1+1..c2-1` to color 4.
3. Do not fill incomplete/open outlines, dangling segments, or cells outside qualifying interiors. Keep all outline cells unchanged. If rectangles share a wall, retain the wall and fill each interior independently.
4. Verify coordinates carefully: the interior begins one row/column after the top/left border and ends one before the bottom/right border. Count rows explicitly to avoid omitting the first interior row or shifting the rectangle by one.
5. Return the full grid at original dimensions; do not assume the background color is 9 or the outline color is 5.

## Evidence and useful variants
- Earlier instance: background 9 and scaffold 5. Three closed rectangles included two adjacent rectangles sharing a vertical boundary and a separate lower rectangle. Only strict interiors were changed to 4; open/incomplete scaffold portions were untouched.
- Later demo: background 9, scaffold 6. Closed rectangles with borders at rows 5–9, columns 9–11 and rows 5–9, columns 24–26 (1-indexed) were filled: their one-cell-wide interiors, rows 6–8 at columns 10 and 25, changed from 9 to 4. A dangling vertical line at column 22 was not filled.

- For degenerate narrow frames, apply the strict-interior rule mechanically; if there are no interior cells, there is nothing to change.
